rubric.why: This states the fraction of pure gold in 22-carat gold.
rubric.description: States that 22 out of 24 parts are gold.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the correct proportion of gold.

rubric.why: The remaining parts are other metals, making the gold an alloy.
rubric.description: States that the remaining 2 parts are other metals.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying the other metals or the remaining proportion.

modelAnswer: 22-carat gold contains 22 parts of pure gold out of 24 parts, so its purity is 22/24.
The remaining 2 parts are other metals, such as copper or silver; therefore, 22-carat gold is an alloy.

items.followUp: Why does atomic radius generally decrease from left to right across a period?

rubric.why: An increase in nuclear charge is the cause of the stronger attraction across a period.
rubric.description: States that nuclear charge increases from left to right.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the increase in nuclear charge.

rubric.why: Stronger attraction makes it harder for an atom to lose an electron, so electropositivity decreases.
rubric.description: Connects the increased attraction to reduced tendency to lose electrons.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for explaining the decreased tendency to lose electrons or the resulting decrease in electropositivity.

modelAnswer: From left to right across a period, nuclear charge increases while the added electrons enter the same main energy level.
The stronger attraction between the nucleus and valence electrons makes them harder to remove; therefore, electropositivity decreases.

items.followUp: Write any five properties of cathode rays.

rubric.why: Canal rays are positively charged and their response to a field shows the nature of their charge.
rubric.description: Gives two valid properties: canal rays carry positive charge and are deflected towards the negative plate in an electric field.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for each of these two properties.

rubric.why: These describe the path and passage of canal rays through the perforated cathode.
rubric.description: Gives two valid properties: they travel in straight lines and pass through holes in the cathode.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for each of these two properties.

rubric.why: The nature of the gas affects the positive ions that form the rays.
rubric.description: States that the charge-to-mass ratio or nature of canal rays depends on the gas in the tube.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for this property.

modelAnswer: Canal rays consist of positively charged particles.
They travel in straight lines.
In an electric field, they are deflected towards the negative plate.
They pass through the holes in a perforated cathode.
Their charge-to-mass ratio depends on the gas present in the discharge tube.

items.followUp: Write the steps for writing the formula of magnesium chloride.

rubric.why: The correct symbols identify the elements in the compound.
rubric.description: Writes the symbols of the elements in the correct order.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for Mg followed by Cl.

rubric.why: The valencies are needed to determine the subscripts.
rubric.description: Writes the correct valencies of the elements.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for Mg valency 2 and Cl valency 1.

rubric.why: Crossing the valencies gives the subscripts in the formula.
rubric.description: Interchanges the valencies and writes them as subscripts.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the criss-cross step.

rubric.why: The final formula must have the simplest whole-number ratio of atoms.
rubric.description: Writes the correctly simplified chemical formula.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for MgCl₂.

modelAnswer: Write the symbols of the elements in the compound: Mg and Cl.
Write their valencies: Mg = 2 and Cl = 1.
Interchange the valencies and write them as subscripts: Mg₁Cl₂.
Remove the subscript 1 to obtain the formula MgCl₂.

items.followUp: Define covalent compounds and describe any four of their properties.

rubric.why: The definition identifies how ionic bonding forms and what holds the compound together.
rubric.description: Defines an ionic compound as one made of oppositely charged ions held together by electrostatic attraction.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a correct definition.

rubric.why: These are characteristic physical properties of ionic compounds.
rubric.description: Gives any two valid properties, such as crystalline nature, high melting or boiling points, or solubility in water.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for each distinct valid property, up to 2 marks.

rubric.why: These further properties distinguish ionic compounds, particularly their electrical behaviour and solubility.
rubric.description: Gives any two additional valid properties, such as electrical conduction when molten or dissolved, no conduction as solids, or insolubility in organic solvents.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for each distinct valid property not already credited, up to 2 marks.

modelAnswer: Ionic compounds are compounds formed by the transfer of electrons from one atom to another; they consist of oppositely charged ions held together by electrostatic forces of attraction.
They are usually crystalline solids.
They generally have high melting and boiling points.
They are usually soluble in water and insoluble in organic solvents.
They do not conduct electricity in the solid state, but conduct electricity when molten or dissolved in water.

items.followUp: Write any four characteristics of a suspension.

rubric.why: A solution has uniform composition throughout.
rubric.description: States that a solution is a homogeneous mixture.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for this characteristic.

rubric.why: A solution is made from a solute dissolved in a solvent.
rubric.description: Identifies the solute and solvent as the components of a solution.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for naming these components.

rubric.why: Solution particles remain dispersed rather than settling on standing.
rubric.description: States that the solute particles do not settle on standing.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for this characteristic.

rubric.why: The dissolved particles are too small to be removed by ordinary filtration.
rubric.description: States that a solution cannot be separated by ordinary filtration.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for this characteristic.

modelAnswer: A solution is a homogeneous mixture with uniform composition throughout.
It consists of a solute dissolved in a solvent.
Its particles do not settle on standing, so the solution is stable.
The dissolved particles pass through filter paper, so the solute cannot be separated by ordinary filtration.

items.followUp: What is the scope of organic chemistry?

rubric.why: This identifies the subject matter of biochemistry.
rubric.description: States that biochemistry studies the chemical substances or processes in living organisms.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the definition or subject matter.

rubric.why: These examples show the fields or biological processes covered by biochemistry.
rubric.description: Gives relevant areas or examples within the scope of biochemistry.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for one or more relevant applications or topics.

modelAnswer: Biochemistry is the branch of chemistry that studies the chemical substances and processes occurring in living organisms.
Its scope includes the study of biomolecules and metabolism, and its knowledge is applied in fields such as medicine, agriculture and food science.

items.followUp: Define molecular formula and give an example.

rubric.why: An empirical formula expresses the simplest ratio of atoms of each element in a compound.
rubric.description: Defines an empirical formula as the simplest whole-number ratio of the atoms of each element in a compound.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the definition.

rubric.why: Glucose has molecular formula C₆H₁₂O₆, whose simplest ratio is CH₂O.
rubric.description: Gives a correct example, such as glucose: molecular formula C₆H₁₂O₆ and empirical formula CH₂O.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a correct example.

modelAnswer: An empirical formula shows the simplest whole-number ratio of the atoms of each element in a compound.
For example, glucose has molecular formula C₆H₁₂O₆ and empirical formula CH₂O.
